title: Using the @extend Directive
ques: Explain the mechanics of the **`@extend`** directive in Sass. Write an example showing an error button sharing base button styles via `@extend`.
explanation: `@extend` tells Sass that one selector should inherit the styles of another. In the compiled CSS, Sass groups selectors (`.button-base, .button-danger { ... }`) to avoid repeating property declarations.

title: Placeholder Selectors (%)
ques: Explain why **Placeholder Selectors (`%`)** are preferable to concrete class selectors when extending styles. Write an example using `%card-layout`.
explanation: Placeholder selectors (`%`) only compile to CSS when extended. Unused placeholders produce zero CSS output, preventing dead code bloat.

title: Chaining Multiple Extends
ques: Demonstrate how a single selector can inherit styles from **multiple extended placeholders** simultaneously.
explanation: A selector can extend multiple placeholders or classes, composing different visual aspects (borders, shapes, layout) cleanly.

title: When to Use Extend vs Mixin
ques: Provide architectural guidelines for deciding between **`@extend`** and **`@mixin`**.

answer.content:
### Decision Matrix:
* **Use `@mixin` when:**
  * Styles require dynamic arguments (e.g., custom colors, font sizes, calculations).
  * Styles are used within distinct `@media` queries.
  * You are writing reusable libraries where relationships between selectors should not be tightly coupled.
* **Use `@extend` (specifically with `%placeholders`) when:**
  * A static group of properties is shared across many classes without varying parameters.
  * You want to group selectors in the compiled CSS (`.btn-a, .btn-b { ... }`) to minimize raw uncompressed CSS file size.

explanation: Mixins duplicate CSS declarations wherever included, but offer parametric flexibility. Extends group selectors without parameters, which can cause bloat if misused across media queries.

title: Limitations and Pitfalls of @extend
ques: Describe the major limitations of `@extend`, specifically its inability to cross `@media` query boundaries.
explanation: Sass forbids extending selectors defined outside a `@media` block from within it, because CSS semantics do not support expressing this relationship without generating invalid selector lists.
